title: Review dispatch: checkpoint-bound findings and a server-side round ceiling

story.i_want_to: place a review as its own dispatch that reads the thread and records findings against a checkpoint
story.so_that: review rounds carry each fix's reasoning, and the round ceiling is enforced from data rather than a per-machine plugin

rationale: PRD §6: round 2 mostly finds defects round 1's fixes introduced; the reviewer lacked the reasoning.

acceptance_criteria.description: A review dispatch kind exists; loopctl places it as a sibling of the implementer's dispatch under the orchestrator's root, never on the implementer's chain and never for a principal that recorded a checkpoint of the thread.
The review payload carries the story, the checkpoint diff reference, the thread's entries, and every fix with the findings it answers.

finding and verdict entries are accepted only from the key a placed review dispatch minted, bound to that dispatch and to the checkpoint it reviews; each review dispatch writes exactly one verdict, and a completed round is that verdict. A dispatch that ends without one uses no round.
A finding carries a severity (critical, high, medium, low) and, after round 1, introduced_by: a checkpoint id of the story at or before the checkpoint it was found in, or none, canonicalised.

A fix entry is accepted only from the current claimant under the current claim_epoch with a live lease, names at least one finding of the story, and is carried by a checkpoint of the current claim recorded after the checkpoints its findings were found in.

A third round is placeable only when a round-2 finding's introduced_by names a checkpoint a round-1 fix references; otherwise, when a round-2 finding of severity critical, high or medium remains, the story escalates with review_ceiling at the end of round 2, and no round 4 is ever placeable.
Refusals on this path never use self_review_blocked, which feeds the L6 custody halt; the judgement kinds' refusals have their own codes.

test_cases.name: only a placed review dispatch judges
steps: finding from the implementer, from a released implementer, from a user key, from the review dispatch

test_cases.name: review payload
preconditions: thread with a round-1 finding and its fix
expected_results: story, checkpoint diff ref, entries, each fix with its findings

test_cases.name: one verdict per dispatch
steps: a second verdict from the same review dispatch; a dispatch released with no verdict

test_cases.name: finding and fix rules
steps: introduced_by after found; fix on an older checkpoint; fix under an ended claim

test_cases.name: ceiling from data
steps: round 2 findings with and without introduced_by on a fix checkpoint
expected_results: round 3 placeable only in the first case; round 4 never; no self_review_blocked

technical_notes: The round count and the ceiling are computed from thread_entries alone, one verdict per review dispatch.
Material means severity critical, high or medium.
The fix rules and the lessons of #901's three review rounds carry over: canonical UUIDs, lease-only liveness, ordering by checkpoint seq, and no key-inferred judge.
